rate.description: The numeric value associated to the rate. In the example of 5 US dollars per hour, the number 5 is the rate value. In the example of 3 bags of rice per month, the number 3 is the rate value. In the example of 20 percent of annual sales, the rate value would be 20.

currencyCode.description: A standard currency code as per ISO 4217. For any given rate, either the currencyCode or the unitCode is present. In the example of 5 US dollars per hour, the unitCode would not be present, and the currency code would be USD.

unitCode.description: For any given rate, either the currencyCode or the unitCode is present. In the example of 3 bags of rice per month, currencyCode would not be present, and the unitCode would be bags of rice. In the example of 20 percent of annual sales, the unitCode would be percent

code.description: The code for the related entity

name.description: The short description of the related code used as a coded name

baseUnitCode.description: For any given rate, the baseUnitCode is used to define the denominator of the rate, or rate over what. In the example of 5 US dollars per hour, the baseUnitCode is hour. In the example of 3 bags of rice per month, the baseUnitCode is month. In the example of 10 US dollars for every widget produced, the baseUnitCode would be widget. In the examplem of 20 percent of annual sales, the baseUnitCode would equate to annual sales.

code.description: The code for the related entity

name.description: The short description of the related code used as a coded name

baseMultiplierValue.description: For any given rate, the base rate value is presumed to be 1, e.g. per one hour, per one month. If for example, the rate was 10 US dollars for every widget produced, the base rate value is presumed to be one and there is no need to communicate a baseMultiplierValue. If however, the rate was 10 US Dollars for every 3 widgets produced, the baseMultiplierValue would be 3,
